population.geography: SF Analysis Neighborhoods: Mission, South of Market and Mission Bay
population.population_scope: Adult residents aged 18+ of Mission, South of Market, Mission Bay

current_citywide_context.status: preliminary state estimate, E-2; not a 2026 count or Census ACS estimate

employment_calibration.source_population: Residents age 16 and over (B23025_001); denominator count not published in this extract
employment_calibration.occupation_dimension: Broad occupation groups, not employer industries
employment_calibration.assumption: Use older 16+ resident status shares as proxies for current-sample 18+ adults, independently of age within neighborhood. Source Unemployment Rate is B23025_005/B23025_001, not the conventional labor-force unemployment rate. Employed proxy = B23025_002/B23025_001 minus B23025_005/B23025_001; it includes Armed Forces, whose occupations are not measured by C24050. Transfer civilian employed occupation shares to the synthetic employed proxy independently of age; these are scenario assignments, not a measured joint distribution.

population.method: Seeded largest remainder: neighborhood adults, then age within neighborhood

sampling_weights.definition: Stratum adult estimate / realized agents; null for an empty stratum

assumptions.individual_age: After stratifying the four broad bands, draw a source sub-band with probabilities proportional to its counts, then an integer age uniformly within it. Ages 75+ use assumed range 75-100; no claim of a measured exact-age distribution.
assumptions.background: All experiences and residence durations are invented scenario facts, independent of demographic identity; no real people or personal records.
assumptions.unmeasured_fields: housing_status is unspecified. No household-tenure marginal is treated as an individual adult's tenure. Employment uses the separately documented older 16+ proxy; occupation_sector means a broad resident occupation group, not an industry.
assumptions.employment: Use older 16+ resident status shares as proxies for current-sample 18+ adults, independently of age within neighborhood. Source Unemployment Rate is B23025_005/B23025_001, not the conventional labor-force unemployment rate. Employed proxy = B23025_002/B23025_001 minus B23025_005/B23025_001; it includes Armed Forces, whose occupations are not measured by C24050. Transfer civilian employed occupation shares to the synthetic employed proxy independently of age; these are scenario assignments, not a measured joint distribution.

population.latest_accessible_note: 2019-2023 is the latest neighborhood age and total vintage exposed in this DataSF dataset at retrieval. Census has released 2020-2024 ACS, but it is not substituted without a verified tract aggregation. These estimates are not current 2026 counts.
limitations: ACS estimates describe a five-year period and carry sampling and nonsampling error; they are not a census of today's residents.
Reported source margins of error are retained; derived broad-band margins use root-sum-squares as an approximation without covariance, and uncertainty in shares is not propagated.
Adult-only simulation excludes ages 0-17 and uses the adult resident denominator; it does not represent families or household structure.
Small samples omit some strata and cannot reproduce the full resident population or support neighborhood behavior inference.
Weights are descriptive expansion factors for represented strata, not survey inclusion probabilities or instructions to multiply agents or API calls.

No race, ethnicity, personality, values, violence propensity, goals, or housing distribution is inferred. Age, employment, and occupation combinations are explicit independence assumptions, not observed joint records.
The simulation geography is a stylized map; official neighborhood totals should not be interpreted as people inside its viewport.

Employment and occupation use 2016-2020 age16+ proxy marginals with no published margins in the extracted profile, applied to 2019-2023 adult calibration; this mixed-vintage independence model cannot reproduce age-specific retirement, unemployment, or occupational patterns.
This is a resident sample; inbound commuters are not yet simulated.
Employer assignments are scenarios, not observed resident-to-employer links.
Industry quotas use citywide workplace jobs as a resident proxy; the occupation-industry joint distribution and named-employer membership are scenario assumptions.
The broader employer reference catalog may include offices outside the resident areas.
Playable streets use official DataSF centerlines with an exaggerated east-west scale; buildings and entrances are synthetic street-adjacent sites, not actual parcels.
Housing capacities, starting credits, wages and schedules are game assumptions.
Public career counterparts are individually sourced; private histories and recent events are labeled fiction, not reconstructed facts about actual people.

person_references.basis: The curated counterpart roster applies to 100-person runs

policy.industry_basis: Hamilton allocation of employed residents using 2025 SF County QCEW workplace jobs as an explicitly imperfect resident-industry proxy; independently assigned from older resident occupation marginals.
policy.named_basis: Requested example quotas are reserved first, then at most one synthetic reference seat per other curated named site within its sector; remaining workers use generic sector facilities. This is an illustrative coverage rule, not company market share or measured staffing.
policy.quota_basis: User-requested three illustrative OpenAI workers and one Anthropic role for public-figure casting, prioritized within technology quota before other reference sites; not measured staff or market share. Small cohorts may supply fewer and disclose the shortfall.
policy.commuting_basis: All assigned workplaces represented on the playable map; no measured commuting or remote-work allocation.

industry_source.scope: San Francisco County covered employer jobs by place of work, including inbound commuters; not employed residents or unique companies.
industry_source.selection: Private ownership 5, aggregation level 74 (NAICS sectors), plus ownership 1/2/3 all-industry totals at level 71; size 0, quarter A, disclosure blank.
